# v1.1.0-dev.88 — Undo in the display editor, and arrow keys that nudge

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.87`.

## Ctrl+Z Works In Display Settings

It did nothing there before. Not the wrong thing, nothing: the undo that
serves the profile editor stands down the moment a dialog opens, which is
right for it. The display editor kept no history of its own. Drag a
monitor somewhere wrong and the only way back was to drag it back by eye.

**Ctrl+Z** and **Ctrl+Y** work inside the dialog now. **Ctrl+Shift+Z**
redoes as well. Moving a display, scaling, orientation, resolution,
refresh rate, the display-only preset, Reset, Save this arrangement,
Remove arrangement and restoring an earlier arrangement are all on the
trail. The editor says which one it took back, under the picture of your
desk:

> Undid: moved a display.

Holding an arrow key is one step rather than thirty. A change that changes
nothing leaves no step, which is why undo never appears to skip one.
Undoing all the way returns exactly the state the dialog opened in, which
is the same promise Cancel makes.

## Arrow Keys Move Things By Pixels

Hold **Shift** and press an arrow in display settings and the selected
display moves 100 pixels. Press it again and it moves another 100. Hold
**Ctrl** as well for a 10 pixel step.

It used to jump the display flush against a side of its nearest
neighbour. That was idempotent. The second press of the same key did
nothing at all, which reads as a key that has stopped working. It also
left no way to slide a display along an edge it already shared.

The layout rules still have the last word. Nudge a display into its
neighbour and it is pushed back out. Nudge it off the desk and it is
docked back on. Those two directions land where they started. Every other
direction moves.

Arrow keys nudge windows in the visual editor too, where they did nothing
before. 10 pixels a press, or 1 with **Shift** held. A nudged window
crosses onto the next monitor exactly the way a dragged one does.

Both canvases are in the keyboard reference that **?** opens, which had
never mentioned either of them.

## Custom Resolutions, And Only Where They Apply

**Add resolutions…** is **Custom resolutions…** now. The dialog behind it
carries that title for every driver instead of naming the vendor. Add
described half of it. That dialog also lists what is already registered
and lets you take one out.

The button appeared whenever the driver was installed, which is not the
same question as whether its display is on the desk. Installed and idle is
the ordinary state between sessions. So every real monitor's card grew a
button offering to add resolutions to a display that was not there. It
appears on that display now, or on any of them where one driver runs
several. With none of them up it appears only where a profile actually
wants a size the driver does not list.

A resolution that reported success and then did not take used to blame "a
known Windows 11 24H2 issue with virtual displays" whatever kind of
display it was. It says that only about a display that is one. Either way
it says what happened before it says why.

## The Lists Fill Their Dialogs

dev.85 claimed this and measured clean, because every list it measured was
empty. A rule set the lists growing. A stronger rule two lines above it
stopped them shrinking. An empty list needs no room to shrink into, which
is why nothing showed. Put forty rows in the History list and it grew to
1201 pixels inside a 579 pixel window, carrying the buttons down to 2623.

The lists scroll now and the buttons stay where they are. Load details was
capped at 320 pixels with 260 pixels of empty window under a list that was
already scrolling. A section with nothing in it no longer holds half the
History dialog open to show one sentence. There is 16 pixels between a
list and the buttons under it, where there was none.

## Padding And Line Length

Every margin, padding and gap in the app is one of twelve values now, down
from twenty-four. The ones that went were the ones used once or twice,
which carry no meaning either way: 11 pixels in three places, 17 pixels in
one. Three pieces of help text ran to 117, 126 and 91 characters a line
against a readable 75. They are capped.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
